question.problem: On average, a wedding dress store sells $9$ wedding dresses per week. What is the probability that the wedding dress store will sell more than $3$ wedding dresses next week? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places. You may assume that wedding dress sales occur independently and at a constant average rate.
question.worked_solution:
A Poisson random variable $X$ with rate $\lambda $ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=\frac{{\lambda }^{x}{e}^{-\lambda }}{x!}
$$

Let $X$ be the number of wedding dresses sold. Since the average rate is $9$ wedding dresses sold per week, and events occur independently and at a constant average rate, the number of wedding dresses sold can be modeled as a Poisson random variable with rate $\lambda =9,$ and we can write $X∼\text{Po}(9).$ 

So, $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=\frac{{9}^{x}{e}^{-9}}{x!}
$$

To compute $P(X>3),$ we will use the complement:

$$
P(X>3)=1-P(X\le 3)
$$

Computing the probability of the complement, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 3) & =P(X\in {0,1,2,3}) \\  & =f(0)+f(1)+f(2)+f(3) \\  & =\frac{{9}^{0}{e}^{-9}}{0!}+\frac{{9}^{1}{e}^{-9}}{1!}+\frac{{9}^{2}{e}^{-9}}{2!}+\frac{{9}^{3}{e}^{-9}}{3!} \\  & ≈0.021\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.

Therefore, the probability of selling more than $3$ wedding dresses next week is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>3) & =1-P(X\le 3) \\  & ≈1-0.021 \\  & =0.979\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
